Rogieria (B37)

Region (English ranking partition): Escann.

In a sentence: Lead the displaced Silmuna remnants from exile to a new kingdom in Escann, then decide what means they will use to return to the imperial throne.

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Very long (66 direct B37 missions) | Mission-tree update: officially released in 2022; current local file modified 2026-09-07 and supports v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: Very high | Tedium: Medium-high | Early pressure: High | Expansion: High

Identity and history

Rogieria (B37) is not a kingdom already established in 1444. You begin instead as the Sons of Dameria (B07), an Escanni adventurer company of East Damerian culture and the Regent Court, led by the exiled Rogier Silmuna. The Lilac Wars destroyed the family’s rule in Dameria; exiles, dispossessed nobles, and their soldiers seek a new home in Escann after the Greentide. Anbenncost, the old capital, remains their homeland in memory, but is not a city a nascent company can immediately reclaim.

There are two Rogiers in this story, and they must not be conflated. The leader in the 1444 history setup is “Rogier the Exiled.” The later Rogier known as “the Young Owl” is Lothane Bluetusk’s son. After B37 forms, a dedicated event introduces the Young Owl as heir or new ruler depending on whether the former is still alive. The offline Wiki also recounts the family story of the exiles founding the company and their successors inheriting the crown, but its fixed dates around 1473 belong to setting lore; the in-game foundation date depends on player conditions.

National story and campaign arc

The first half asks how to survive in a new land. The Sons of Dameria must secure a foothold in West Castanor, settle, form Rogieria, and rebuild the towns, fortifications, and farmland of the Taran Plains. The new kingdom inherits Dameria’s lunar heraldry but faces the reality of Adenica’s former knightly lands and the Escanni survivors: is it old Dameria transplanted east, or a genuinely new Escanni state? The Young Owl’s reputation, the Farrani crown, and family stories of ancestors turn that question into a continuing political choice.

Only in the second half does the return home begin. Rogieria gathers Silmuna relics, courts old friends, mages, and princes, and organizes the Shadowmoon Conspiracy to make Anbenncost and the old lands of Dameria recognize the family’s claim again. The imperial throne cannot be won by one war alone: diplomatic standing, spy networks, allies’ positions, and conquest can all shape the return. The tree’s end seeks to put a Silmuna back on the Dove Throne. This is a future the player may pursue, not an established fact in 1444.

Core mechanics

  1. Two-stage national identity: B07 claims land as an adventurer company and meets the settlement-reform and administrative-technology requirements; forming B37 changes the Tag and grants its dedicated missions. The count of 66 covers Rogieria’s direct missions, not the predecessor’s generic adventurer missions.
  2. Three Silmuna legacies: Missions and events separately accumulate tendencies toward an “Autocratic Monarch,” a “Beloved by the People” ruler, or a “Restoration of the Old Order.” How you govern the frontier and treat the crown and old retainers shapes the Young Owl’s long-term political image and related rewards. These are not three entirely isolated countries.
  3. Shadowmoon Conspiracy: In the mid-to-late campaign, missions recruit imperial princes and use diplomacy, espionage, or force against those who will not cooperate. This creates a gradual political route for returning home rather than simply pressing permanent claims.
  4. A new half-orc identity: Lothane Bluetusk’s Silmuna line brings half-orcs into the royal family and army. Related missions call for half-orc culture advisors, tolerance, and settlements, and portray them as farmers, scholars, and citizens—not merely expendable soldiers.
  5. Reconstruction and frontier defense: Old towns and forts such as Taranton and Balmire, along with neglected land, need restoration. Trade, tea, workshops, fortifications, and artillery support later wars across Escann and the Empire.

Campaign by phase

Survive the opening. The Sons of Dameria face competition for land in post-Greentide Escann. Secure the West Castanor territory needed to settle, advance the adventurer reforms, then meet the peace and administrative-technology requirements to form Rogieria. Fixating too early on reclaiming Dameria means neglecting the population, income, and defenses the new kingdom needs.

After forming B37, expand while investing in the Taran Plains and northern fortresses to shore up the Young Owl’s political base. Missions ask for family honor, urban reconstruction, half-orc integration, and Corinite faith; some goals reward patient development, while others require war. Near the imperial phase, cultivate relations with princes in the old lands and advance the Shadowmoon Conspiracy. Player posts describe bankruptcies partway through, but those are individual campaign outcomes, not a fixed mechanic of the tree.

Formation and endgame

B07 Sons of Dameria → B37 Rogieria is the continuous campaign chain covered here. Later, Rogieria may separately meet the generic requirements to form Dameria (A58), changing Tag again and switching mission trees. A58 is an optional detour, not part of B37’s missions; nor does Rogieria automatically become A58 simply by calling itself “East Dameria.” Alternatively, retain B37 and contest the imperial throne, making the new kingdom—not the old country name—the answer to Silmuna restoration.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 85/100 | Authoritarianism 60/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 24/100) | Pluralism 75/100.

The v2.1 values rating is Good (82/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory. Half-orcs are explicitly integrated as farmers, scholars, citizens, and advisors, and the story includes clemency and a beloved-ruler path. Dynastic restoration and the imperial claim principally affect expansion and authoritarianism and should not be counted against values a second time.

Recommended for players who enjoy character-driven succession, an exile’s restoration, diplomatic intrigue, and long-term imperial politics. If you dislike the early land-grab in Escann, cross-region objectives, construction costs, and complicated family events, Rogieria is much harder than the slogan “reclaim the crown” suggests.

Community experience and evidence limits

The 2022 official dev diary describes the Young Owl, Silmuna legacies, and Shadowmoon Conspiracy; the release announcement that year confirms Rogieria’s tree went live, and later hotfixes adjusted mission requirements. Two player posts report that the legacy paths chiefly affect national character and rewards; a player who completed the first half praised the family narrative while also describing defeat in religious war and bankruptcy. These are experiences from their respective versions. Current identity, conditions, and missions are governed by the local Mod and localisation. Later Wiki dates and territorial reconstructions in community history maps are not inevitable outcomes of a campaign.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Rogieria (B37) — Rogierian Ideas

Set ID: B37_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B37
    }

Rogierian Traditions

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

1. Last Blood of Silmuna

At the end of the Lilac Wars in 1443 one of the last remaining Silmunas, Rogier Silmuna, son of Adenn Skylance and rightful heir to the Grand Duchy of Dameria and the Empire of Anbennar, had no choice but to flee his homeland and seek shelter amongst the marcher lords that made their way to Escann to fight the Greentide.

The heirs of Rogieria share blood with Rogier, and claim themselves as the last true Silmunas in Anbennar, as their Wesdamerian cousins had fought against Dameria in the war.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

2. Sons of Dameria

The Sons of Dameria were composed of exiled soldiers and nobility that once served under Grand Duchy of Dameria. Resigned to their fate as losers of the war, many sought a new life of valour elsewhere in fighting the Greentide.

By the 1800s these men and women who lost everything and proceeded to fight for a place that held no stake to them was one of the main catalysts for the Romantic movement.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

3. Connections within the Old Empire

Despite their self-imposed exile, many important members of Rogieria still hold family ties to those remaining in Anbennar and the rest of Cannor. Ties that can be called upon for Rogieria's gain.

  • Diplomatic relations: +2 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 2).

4. The Cult of Rogier

Many years after Rogier's death a man named Owen the Mad began to rave about how Rogier was one of the most important and best Silmunas around. This eventually spread across Rogieria and reinforced the idea of Silmuna hegemony and the quasi-worship of Rogier within Rogierian beliefs and traditions, much to the dismay of its neighbours.

  • Ruler administrative skill: +1 (monarch_admin_power; raw value 1).

5. Reclaim What is Ours

"Reclaim What Is Ours" -House Words of the Rogierian Silmunas

Long scorned from their homeland, the King Ellís of Rogieria eventually made peace with the Wesdamerian branch of the family and joined houses with his marriage with Duchess Laurentíne. Years later he infamously tried to reclaim the Grand Duchy of Dameria and lost Wesdam's lands in Madelaire - after that his son Lothane II fought for much of his short life to defend his territories but eventually lost both Wesdam and Rogieria by 1582.

  • Aggressive expansion impact: -15% (ae_impact; raw value -0.15).

6. Roaring Batteries of Rogieria

Rogierian forces often had to face larger numbers and such developed an intricate and terrifying artillery device that guaranteed the fledgling kingdom's independence for many years.

  • Land fire damage: +10% (fire_damage; raw value 0.1).

7. Shadowmoon Conspiracy

Named after the Rogierian flag which contains the elven moon on black, the Shadowmoon Conspiracy is allegedly a hidden network of Silmuna loyalists that plot to put a Silmuna back on the imperial throne of Anbennar.

  • Spy network construction: +20% (spy_offence; raw value 0.2).

Rogierian Ambition

  • Leader land fire: +1 (leader_land_fire; raw value 1).

Dameria (A58) — Damerian Ideas

Set ID: A58_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A58 #Dameria
    }

Damerian Traditions

  • Chance of a new heir: +50% (heir_chance; raw value 0.5).

  • Improve relations: +30% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.3).

1. Imperial Sovereignty

The Silmunas have sat on the imperial throne of Anbennar for much of its history, and by the graces of the gods an Anbennar without a Silmuna is no Anbennar at all.

  • Imperial authority growth modifier: +0.1 (imperial_authority; raw value 0.1).

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

2. Wooden Wall of Damesear

Dameria's position as lord of the Damesear has allowed it to become a great power across all of Cannor, but to protect the isle from any would-be invaders it must be protected by a wooden wall: the finest ships in the Dameshead.

  • Galley construction cost: -15% (galley_cost; raw value -0.15).

  • Galley Combat Ability: +20% (galley_power; raw value 0.20).

3. Damerian Court Conduct

Most royal courts in history were modeled of the Damerian Court during the Interregnum where we established properly court conduct, etiquette and ceremony.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +200% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 2).

4. Silmuna School of the Arts

Founded in 1024, the Silmuna School is one of the most prestigious institutions of magic, sciences and arts in all of Cannor.

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

5. Damerian Adventurer Companies

Dameria won its wars due to their adventurer irregulars, whom often found a home in Anbenncóst or as newly found nobility under the kingdom.

  • Mercenary Cost: -15% (mercenary_cost; raw value -0.15).

  • Mercenary Discipline: +10% (mercenary_discipline; raw value 0.1).

6. Legacy of the Damerian Republic

Before the Grand Duchy was the Kingdom, and before the Kingdom was the Republic: the ancient force that civilized all of Cannor and made it what it is today.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

7. Anbenncóst, the City of the World's Desire

At the highest hill of Anbenncóst sits the Imperial Palace, formerly the Damerian Palace. Though no doubt, the strength of Dameria lies not in its diplomacy, nor its traditions, but the people of Anbenncóst that form the foundation of all things right.

  • Domestic trade power: +20% (global_own_trade_power; raw value 0.2).
